title: The Twelvefold Binding and Release of the Soul in the Body
arc: The teaching traces how the soul, taken from the five radiant Sons of the First Man, is bound faculty-by-faculty into the five somatic substrates of a body that Sin has fashioned from the Five Worlds of Darkness, and how the Mind of Light then unbinds each captive faculty, rebinds Sin's counterpart in its place, and constitutes the freed members as the New Man — even while the Mind of Light himself remains hidden and shrunken within the body's narrow watch-posts.
reading:
This chapter sets out the whole anatomy of captivity and regeneration as a single mechanical sequence inside the human form. Its starting premise is that the cosmos itself stands established by the Living Spirit working through all his members; the human body is a microcosm of that same architecture, but built by the opposing hand. Sin took this body forth from the Land of Darkness, fashioning it out of the five bodies of Darkness (the Five Worlds of self-love), and established his own five members — the five-fold proprium — within it. Into that prepared structure the soul was taken, drawn down from the five radiant Gods (the Five Sons of the First Man, the descending attributes of Divine Truth), and bound member by member into the somatic frame.

The teaching then gives the precise correspondence between the five intellectual faculties and the five bodily substrates that imprison them: the **mind** is bound in **bone** (structural good captured by Sin's framework), **thought** in **sinew** (the conducting power of truth held in Sin's strength), **teaching** in **vein** (doctrine running in Sin's channels), **counsel** in **flesh** (deliberative wisdom mired in concupiscence), and **reflection** in **skin** (inner discrimination reduced to mere surface). Worse than this nesting, Sin sets his own counter-faculty upon each of the soul's faculties — his mind upon her mind, his thought upon her thought, and so on — so that with five governing exousiastai he overlays and oppresses every receptive opening of the soul. Drawn at every hour to evil works and to the sins of desire, the soul dons Error and Forgetfulness as her garment, forgets her own substance, her kind, and her manner, and no longer knows the door of her Father's dwelling-place by which she might call upward. She becomes enemy to her Father — the classical Manichaean image of the Living Soul utterly mingled in the body and ignorant of her origin.

The middle of the teaching is the redemptive reversal, given as a clean inverse of the binding. The Lord (here operative as the Mind of Light, with Jesus the Radiance implicit behind him) goes through the five substrates one by one and performs a double action at each: he **raises and releases** the soul-faculty out of its substrate, and **binds** Sin's corresponding faculty into that same substrate in its place. Mind is raised out of bone and Sin's mind is bound there; thought released from sinew, Sin's thought bound there; teaching released from vein, Sin's teaching bound there; counsel released from flesh, Sin's counsel bound there; reflection released from skin, Sin's reflection bound there. The bones, sinews, veins, flesh, and skin are not destroyed but reassigned: what once held the soul captive now becomes the prison of the proprium. The freed members of the soul are then refined, gathered, and established as the **New Man**, the son of Righteousness.

Upon this regenerated frame the Lord places five great living members corresponding to the five faculties, and the chapter names the celestial qualities that fill them: in the new mind, **love**; in the new thought, **faith**; in the new teaching, what the lacuna leaves implicit but is plainly the third virtue (perfection, named just below in the parallel list); in the new counsel, **patience**; in the new reflection, **wisdom**. The image of the soul's speech is purified out of the speech of Sin and the Lord's own speech is added within it, so that his word becomes the soul's nourisher and strengthener. Together with the five somatic substrates (now turned into prisons of Sin's faculties) and the five regenerated faculties of the New Man, the title's "twelve members" stand fulfilled — completeness in church, the full zodiacal articulation of the regenerate human, with the soul running back along its road to the great Aeons of the height.

The closing movement of the teaching faces honestly the unfinished character of this regeneration in the present life. Two states now coexist in the body. On one hand, the Old Man is bound in his desire, greed, and foolishness in the five members of the body, and the spirit of darkness is mingled inward with him in a strong distress. On the other hand, the New Man reigns in love, faith, perfection, patience, and wisdom, and the **Mind of Light reigns over the All** within him. But Sin, though bound, is not extinct: there are times when Sin ascends in his foolishness, stirs up the reflection, confounds the wisdom and prudence of the man, snatches the truth (which is separation, the discriminating power) out of his hand into double-mindedness, and proclaims words bitter and salt — the salt-sea taste of the mingled state breaking through.

To explain why the regenerate state can be so disturbed, the teacher draws a remarkable correspondential analogy. Just as the great gods stand fast in the Zone of the cosmos but are not manifest forth from it — held in the cosmic girdle, hidden behind the firmament — and just as the Watchers stand likewise fixed and unseen, so too the Mind of Light, who is in himself great and lofty, stands fixed within the body but is not manifest forth in it. The great Mind has had to **bend down and shrink** to suit the little body that has been fashioned forth, contracting himself against the matter to which he is joined, exactly as the cosmic powers contract themselves against the bulk of the world. This is "the secrecy and the shame of the Mind of Light" — how great he truly is, yet without all the watch-stations of the body, fallen at the feet of his own array, while all the reflections of the body lie shut away from the snares of Sin. By his heart's purpose he constrains those snares, scatters them forth, and sets the soul's members upon their feet. And the chapter signals that one further thing remains to be said, "yet another thing surpassing even more" — the teaching breaks off pointing beyond itself to a still higher mystery of this hidden reign.

The whole arc, then, is a single anatomical drama of regeneration. The body is the contested instrument. Its five substrates are the fixed somatic frame in which either the soul's faculties or Sin's faculties must be lodged; the question is only which is bound where. The Lord's redemptive operation is a precise faculty-by-faculty exchange that turns the prison inside out, then refurnishes the freed faculties with the five virtues of the New Man, completing the twelvefold ordering of the regenerate human. Yet the present condition of even the regenerate is one in which the great Mind of Light is forced to dwell in disguise, contracted and unmanifest, governing through hidden watch-posts rather than open splendour — a hiddenness that mirrors the way the heavenly powers themselves are held in the Zone of the cosmos until the consummation.

major_images.image: the five bodies of the Darkness from which Sin fashions the body, and the five radiant Gods (Sons of the First Man) from whom the soul is taken
major_images.meaning: the two opposing fivefold sources — the five modes of self-love that constitute the somatic frame, and the five attributes of Divine Truth that constitute the soul

major_images.image: the binding of mind in bone, thought in sinew, teaching in vein, counsel in flesh, reflection in skin
major_images.meaning: each intellectual faculty imprisoned in the somatic substrate that corresponds to it, with Sin's own counter-faculty set as overlord upon each one

major_images.image: the Lord raising each faculty out of its substrate and binding Sin's corresponding faculty in its place
major_images.meaning: regeneration as a precise inverse exchange: the same somatic structure is reassigned, becoming the prison of the proprium rather than of the soul

major_images.image: the five virtues placed in the New Man — love in mind, faith in thought, perfection in teaching, patience in counsel, wisdom in reflection
major_images.meaning: the five faculties of the regenerate self filled with the corresponding heavenly goods, completing the twelvefold articulation of the New Man

major_images.image: the great Mind of Light bent down and shrunk to fit the little body, hidden behind the body's watch-posts as the gods are hidden in the Zone
major_images.meaning: the divine governance of the regenerate is real but concealed: the inmost rational reigns over the All while remaining unmanifest in ultimates, mirroring the hiddenness of the heavenly powers within the cosmic girdle

major_images.image: Sin sometimes ascending, stirring the reflection, confounding wisdom, and proclaiming words bitter and salt
major_images.meaning: the residual mingling that breaks through even after regeneration — the salt-sea taste of the unfinished cosmos still active in the body
